title: Rate Card Note — What Each Credited Alarm Is Credited At Where Critical Alarms Have Run

# Rate Card Note — What Each Credited Alarm Is Credited At Where Critical Alarms Have Run

**The step.** Where the twelve months to the handling day carry three or more alarms classed as critical on a plan under the Building Automation Service Plans and the tier includes an after-hours call-out on a critical alarm, each alarm credited is credited at the tier's alarm response overage fee raised by twenty-five per cent. Where the twelve months to the handling day carry three or more alarms classed as critical and the tier includes no after-hours call-out on a critical alarm, each alarm credited is credited at that fee raised by ten per cent. In every other case each alarm credited is credited at the tier's alarm response overage fee. The raised figure is taken to two decimal places.

| Alarms classed as critical in the twelve months to the handling day | Tier includes an after-hours call-out on a critical alarm | Each alarm credited is credited at |
|---|---|---|
| 3 or more | yes | the tier's alarm response overage fee raised by 25 per cent |
| 3 or more | no | the tier's alarm response overage fee raised by 10 per cent |
| fewer than 3 | either | the tier's alarm response overage fee |

## Points of judgement

- The count is of alarms classed as critical raised in the twelve months, acknowledged or not; exactly 3 meets the first two rows.
- Worked figure (hypothetical): at a tier whose alarm response overage fee is 125 USD and which includes the after-hours call-out, a plan with 4 critical alarms in the twelve months credits each alarm at 125 USD raised by 25 per cent, that is 156.25 USD. At a tier of the same fee including no after-hours call-out, each is credited at 137.50 USD.
